title: Dual Quaternion Skinning Comparison Viewer
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a dual quaternion skinning comparison viewer. The scene shows two identical animated humanoid arm meshes side by side — one using standard Linear Blend Skinning (LBS) and one using Dual Quaternion Skinning (DQS) — so the user can visually compare artifacts like candy-wrapper collapse.

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (#1a1a2e). A PerspectiveCamera at (0, 1.5, 4) looking at origin.
- Two directional lights: one from (5,5,5) intensity 1.0, one from (-3,3,-2) intensity 0.5. Ambient light intensity 0.3.
- Create two identical procedural skinned meshes representing a simplified arm (a cylinder-like geometry with ~40 segments along its length, ~16 radial segments). Each arm has 3 bones arranged vertically: shoulder (y=0), elbow (y=1), wrist (y=2). Skin weights blend smoothly between adjacent bones.
- Left arm (centered at x=-1.2) uses standard Linear Blend Skinning (THREE.Skeleton default).
- Right arm (centered at x=+1.2) uses Dual Quaternion Skinning. Implement DQS in a custom ShaderMaterial that reads bone matrices, converts them to dual quaternions, and blends in dual quaternion space before transforming vertices. The vertex shader must implement proper dual quaternion blending with antipodality correction (ensure shortest path).
- Label each arm with a floating HTML overlay div: 'Linear Blend (LBS)' on the left, 'Dual Quaternion (DQS)' on the right.

## Animation & Poses
- Support 4 named poses selectable by the user: 'rest' (all bones identity), 'bend_45' (elbow rotated 45° around Z), 'bend_90' (elbow rotated 90° around Z), 'twist_180' (wrist rotated 180° around its local Y axis — this is the candy-wrapper stress test).
- When a pose is selected, smoothly interpolate from the current pose to the target pose over 0.5 seconds using quaternion slerp on each bone.
- Both arms always animate to the same target pose simultaneously.

## Playback & Auto-Rotate
- A 'Play Sequence' button cycles through all 4 poses in order (rest → bend_45 → bend_90 → twist_180 → rest), holding each pose for 1.5 seconds before transitioning to the next.
- A 'Toggle Auto-Rotate' button enables/disables slow camera orbit around the Y axis (0.3 rad/s).

## Volume Preservation Metric
- For each arm, compute an approximate volume metric: sum the signed volumes of all mesh triangles (using the divergence theorem / signed tetrahedra method) each frame during animation. Normalize relative to the rest-pose volume so rest = 1.0.
- Display the volume ratio for each arm in a HUD panel at the top: 'LBS Volume: X.XXX' and 'DQS Volume: X.XXX'.
- The DQS arm should preserve volume better (closer to 1.0) especially during twist_180.

## Interaction
- Keyboard '1','2','3','4' select poses rest, bend_45, bend_90, twist_180 respectively.
- Keyboard 'P' triggers Play Sequence.
- Keyboard 'R' toggles auto-rotate.
- Mouse drag (left button) orbits camera via OrbitControls.
- A dropdown <select> element also allows pose selection.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- currentPose: string ('rest'|'bend_45'|'bend_90'|'twist_180')
- targetPose: string (the pose being transitioned to)
- isAnimating: boolean (true during pose transition)
- isSequencePlaying: boolean
- autoRotate: boolean
- lbsVolume: number (current normalized volume of LBS arm)
- dqsVolume: number (current normalized volume of DQS arm)
- elapsedTime: number (total elapsed seconds)
- boneRotations: { shoulder: {x,y,z,w}, elbow: {x,y,z,w}, wrist: {x,y,z,w} } (current quaternion values of the bones)
- transitionProgress: number (0 to 1 during animation, 1 when settled)
- sequenceStep: number (0-3 index into pose sequence during playback, -1 when not playing)
- frameCount: number
- cameraDistance: number (distance from camera to origin)
- meshCount: number (total skinned meshes in scene, should be 2)
physics_constraints: Volume preservation: DQS normalized volume must remain within [0.95, 1.05] for all poses. LBS volume may drop below 0.85 during twist_180. Bone quaternions must always be unit quaternions (magnitude within [0.999, 1.001]). Transition progress must be monotonically non-decreasing from 0 to 1 during animation. Camera distance must remain positive and finite.
